scenes.title: What is an Algorithm?
scenes.learning_objective: Understand what an algorithm is and how data structures help programs run faster.
scenes.narration: An algorithm is like a recipe that tells a computer exactly what steps to follow to solve a problem. A data structure is like a special way to organize data so that the algorithm can use it efficiently. Choosing the right algorithm and data structure can make a program run thousands of times faster.
scenes.key_fact: Algorithms are step-by-step recipes; data structures organize data for efficient use.

elements.description: A step-by-step recipe for solving a problem.
A way to organize data so it can be used efficiently.
How fast a program runs depends on the algorithm and data structure used.

scenes.title: Searching: Linear vs Binary Search
scenes.learning_objective: Understand how linear and binary search work and why binary search is faster.
scenes.narration: Linear search checks each item one by one, like looking through a book from the first page. Binary search is much faster, but it only works on a sorted list. It checks the middle item, and if it's not the target, it throws away half the list and repeats. This makes binary search much more efficient.
scenes.key_fact: Binary search is faster because it halves the list each time.

elements.description: Checks each item one by one from the start.
Works on sorted lists and halves the list each time.
A list that is arranged in order for binary search to work.
A list that is not in order, which only works for linear search.

scenes.title: Stacks and Queues
scenes.learning_objective: Understand how stacks and queues work and their common uses.
scenes.narration: A stack is like a pile of plates: you push a plate on top and pop it from the top, so the last plate in is the first one out. Stacks are used for undo buttons and function calls. A queue is like a line at a shop: you add items to the back and remove them from the front, so the first item in is the first out. Queues are used for scheduling tasks and print jobs.
scenes.key_fact: Stacks use LIFO (last in, first out); queues use FIFO (first in, first out).

elements.description: A structure where items are added and removed from the top.
A structure where items are added to the back and removed from the front.
Last in, first out: the last item added is the first one removed.
First in, first out: the first item added is the first one removed.
